method: Model a tight, evenly wound strip as paper filling the annulus between the core and the finished outside diameter. With strip length L, paper caliper t, core diameter c and outside diameter D in one consistent length unit, D = sqrt(c² + 4Lt/π), or L = π(D² − c²)/(4t). Approximate turns are (D − c)/(2t). Strip width does not enter the face-diameter calculation. In target mode D must exceed c. Stock pieces per coil are ceil(L/stock length), with a 12-decimal ratio rounding guard at exact boundaries; joins per coil are one fewer, and offcut is the stock allocated to one coil minus L. Project totals multiply per-coil length and stock pieces by the matching-coil count without sharing offcuts. Decimal inputs are strict: metric caliper 0.05–1 mm, core 0–50 mm, strip 1–10000 mm, target 1–60 mm, stock 10–2000 mm; separate inch bounds are shown in the core. Matching coils are whole numbers 1–100. Results are rounded to four decimals, turns and displayed figures to two (up to three for inch display). The ideal annulus excludes tension, gaps, glue and springback. The page computes in the browser, stores nothing and makes no network requests.
